messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: ggExtra and gridExtra
parts:
Dear list,

Let me apologize for this is almost off-topic, but following an
off-line suggestion I renamed the packages ggextra and gridextra to
ggExtra and gridExtra respectively. This is to maintain a consistent
naming scheme following latticeExtra and zooExtra.

I take this opportunity to explain how these two packages relate to ggplot2,

- gridExtra (http://code.google.com/p/gridextra/) provides
experimental grobs ("graphical objects" for Grid graphics), including
so far: tableGrob (display a data.frame), barbedGrob (points and lines
as in type = 'b'). It also provides an arrange() function to
conveniently place ggplot2 objects and grobs on a page (a wrapper
around grid.layout).

- ggExtra (http://code.google.com/p/ggextra/) provides (highly)
experimental geoms and scales for ggplot2. Currently this includes:

scales:
scale_colour_dichromat(),

geoms:
"geom_ellipse" "geom_field" "geom_fielduv" "geom_ngon" "geom_star"

themes:
"theme_bb" "theme_bw2" "theme_dark" "theme_flashy" "theme_gray2"
"theme_minimal" "theme_talk"


Needless to say, participation is very welcome!

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: ggExtra and gridExtra
parts:
Hi,

Indeed, the binaries on r-forge usually lag by a day or two because
they are built overnight on their servers (and an additional delay
occurs if one gets things wrong with dependencies etc. --- and i often
do)

You can always find the most recent source code on googlecode, either
packaged for Unix systems in the Downloads area, or through anonymous
svn checkout.

Best,

baptiste
